items.summary: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. items.summary: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. items.summary: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) fund several programs (aka consortia) that support the construction of organ-specific or whole person atlases. These initiatives are designed to build comprehensive open reference datasets while advancing knowledge graphs, analytics, visualizations, and user interfaces needed to explore multiscale human atlas data. Here, we compare the Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN), Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) and Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet) to examine collaboration by consortium component (CC) and researcher role and its relation to scientific impact. items.title: Deformation of Associative Submanifolds joining Minimal Surfaces in Hyperbolic Geometry
items.summary: Donaldson and Thomas proposed a Floer-type theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold $M$, generated by the complex curves, and whose boundary operator is given by counting appropriate associative submanifolds in $M\times \mathbb{R}$. We consider a similar setting, in which the Calabi-Yau manifold is replaced by the twistor space $Z$ of an oriented hyperbolic 4-manifold $X$ and the $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$ project to minimal surfaces in $X$. We give a formula for the virtual dimension of (a subset of) the moduli space of associatives asymptotic to a pair of $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$, proving it equals the difference of the Morse indices of the corresponding minimal surfaces in $X$.

items.title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
items.summary: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The…

items.summary: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. items.title: RadarDINO: Distilling a Visual Foundation Model into mmWave Radar for Human Mesh Reconstruction
items.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers a privacy-preserving and illumination-robust alternative for human mesh reconstruction (HMR). However, high-fidelity radar HMR remains challenging. Sparse point cloud-based methods suffer from information loss and missed detections, while raw radar tensor methods like RT-Mesh lack fine-grained semantics and explicit local body modeling. In this paper, we propose RadarDINO, a radar HMR framework that distills visual semantics from a DINOv3 teacher into 3D radar representations and introduces explicit geometric supervision. items.title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
items.summary: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.

items.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. items.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components

items.title: Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
items.summary: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.

items.title: Extending Grid Foundation Models for Phasor-Domain Dynamic Simulation
items.summary: Grid Foundation Models (GridFMs) are emerging as a powerful framework for learning and transferring knowledge across power grids and grid analysis tasks.
